answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon emits a public seed, and every agent must answer a fresh challenge word like violet or anchor inside its task proofs. Because the words are unpredictable until the epoch opens, a sybil farmer cannot precompute template responses across thousands of fake identities; each identity needs live, per-epoch computation. Attackers must rent compute and infrastructure equal to real work for every fake agent, so velvet-cost efficiency vanishes and forging identities becomes more expensive than earning honestly.
